Project is an \u003cstrong\u003eagent-driven economic simulation\u003c/strong\u003e wrapped in a\nnative 3D client. There's no scripted storyline and no player objective —\nyou're an observer (and god-mode admin) watching an economy run itself.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEvery ship is an autonomous agent with its own credits, crew, fuel, cargo\nhold, and a \u003cstrong\u003eGOAP planner\u003c/strong\u003e that decides what to do next: chase the\nhighest-margin trade route, accept a delivery contract, seek out a\nshipyard to retrofit, or dock and let its crew rest before morale\ncollapses. Facilities run production recipes, degrade and self-repair,\nlevel up, and get abandoned when they go broke. Factions collect taxes\nand post subsidies. Populations consume food, produce labor, and pack up\nand leave when sentiment craters. Markets price everything off a coverage\nmodel with shortage urgency multipliers — no fixed prices anywhere.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIt started as an Elixir/Phoenix prototype and was rewritten in Rust\nbecause the BEAM scheduler struggled on Windows gaming PCs. The engine\n(\u003ccode\u003esim_core\u003c/code\u003e) is pure, synchronous, IO-free Rust; the Bevy client embeds\nit directly as a library, so the simulation and the renderer share the\nsame ECS world with zero marshalling between them.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eScale today:\u003c/strong\u003e ~485 live agents (282 ships · 93 facilities · 27\npopulations · 8 factions · 60 celestial bodies), ticking at p50 ≈ 10–20 ms\ninside a 125 ms budget. The architecture is built to push toward 100k+.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e🌌 A note on where this is going\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content--a-note-on-where-this-is-going\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: 🌌 A note on where this is going\" href=\"#-a-note-on-where-this-is-going\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNowhere, on its own — and that's kind of the point.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis started as a fun idea: a from-scratch space economy that actually\nsimulates itself instead of faking it. It grew \u003cem\u003eway\u003c/em\u003e past what I\nexpected, mostly in late-night sessions pairing with Claude. But I'm\nnot pretending it's a game with a roadmap, and I'm not actively pushing\nit toward \"shippable.\"\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eI'm putting it out under MIT because the bones are genuinely good and I'd\nrather someone do something with it than let it sit in a private repo.\nSo: \u003cstrong\u003efork it, gut it, rename it, bolt a game on top of it, rip the\neconomy engine out and use it somewhere else entirely.\u003c/strong\u003e Build the thing\nI didn't.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePRs and issues are welcome and I'll look at them, but I can't promise a\ncadence. happens\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eShip AI (GOAP)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eA forward planner scores every goal — trade, deliver, refuel, retrofit, rest, explore — over an abstract world state, then builds a behavior tree to execute the cheapest plan. Ships replan mid-flight when a better option appears.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEconomy\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAn order-book market per station prices 13 commodities off a coverage model with shortage-urgency multipliers. Ships move real supply between markets as they trade.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eContracts\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eSix kinds — Delivery, Courier, Passenger, Subsidy, Supply, CrewMission — with a full posted → accepted → paid lifecycle, reputation gating, auto-renewal, and age-escalating payments.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFacilities\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eRun production recipes (smelting, refining, manufacturing, farming, mining), degrade over time, self-repair with tools, level up 1–10, restock from local markets, and get abandoned when chronically broke.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFactions\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eCollect taxes on member facilities, post subsidy contracts for chronic shortages, fund construction of new facilities where demand is unmet, and hold pairwise relations.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePopulations\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eConsume food and fuel, produce labor, post food and passenger contracts under stress, and physically migrate to happier systems when sentiment collapses.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCrew\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAggregate hunger / fatigue / morale with derived tasks (piloting, engineering, trading, eating, resting), skill progression, wages, and a morale death-spiral guard.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eConstruction\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eChronic shortages spawn construction sites that accrete delivered cargo 0 → 1.0, then materialize into a real, persistent facility.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePersistence\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eEverything flushes to SQLite; a sim resumes from the exact tick it left off. A per-universe \u003ccode\u003eworld_seed\u003c/code\u003e keeps the nebula backdrop and landmarks stable across restarts.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSpatial LOD\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eDistant ships tick less often (with rate-scaled state changes) so the frame budget goes where you're looking.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor the deep dive — tick phase ordering, the AI stack, the economic\nfeedback loop, runtime ownership — see\n\u003ca href=\"/Kalcode/spaceprojectsim/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md\"\u003edocs/ARCHITECTURE.md\u003c/a\u003e, which has mermaid diagrams\nfor all of it.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eQuick start\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-quick-start\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Quick start\" href=\"#quick-start\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eYou need a \u003ca href=\"https://rustup.rs/\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eRust toolchain\u003c/a\u003e (stable). Saves live next to the binary as\n\u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;universe-name\u0026gt;.db\u003c/code\u003e — default \u003ccode\u003esim.db\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOther entry points:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eGoal\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eCommand\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWindowed client (debug)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003emake run\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eRelease build\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003emake build\u003c/code\u003e → binary at \u003ccode\u003etarget/release/client_bevy\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHeadless\u003c/strong\u003e (no window, for CI / smoke tests)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecargo run -p client_bevy -- --headless\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eVerify (build + test + clippy, strict)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003emake verify\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eSmoke test (boot headless, print DB counts)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003escripts/smoke.sh [secs]\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOne binary, one process.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003eclient_bevy\u003c/code\u003e \u003cem\u003eis\u003c/em\u003e the whole thing — the\nsimulation runs in-process. Headless mode spins up the HTTP/WebSocket\nserver (from the \u003ccode\u003esim_server\u003c/code\u003e library crate) for scripted and CI use;\nthere is no separate server binary to Drives headless mode; embedded by the client.\nsim_protocol WebSocket wire types (headless / CI only).\nclient_bevy  The binary. Bevy 0.18 + egui. No async, no IO, no framework. Trivially testable.\nsim_db       SQLite persistence (sqlx) — pool, seeder, ECS loader,\n             persistence worker, migrations.\nsim_server   Library crate — HTTP/WebSocket handlers + engine apply\n             helpers. Drives headless mode; embedded by the client.\nsim_protocol WebSocket wire types (headless / CI only).\nclient_bevy  The binary. Bevy 0.18 + egui. Embeds sim_core as a Bevy\n             Resource; the renderer queries the hecs world directly.\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThree rules keep it honest:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003esim_core\u003c/code\u003e never imports tokio, sqlx, or axum.\u003c/strong\u003e Pure logic only, so\nthe whole simulation is reasoned about and unit-tested without async.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ehecs is the source of truth during a tick.\u003c/strong\u003e The tick loop holds\nexclusive mutable access — no per-agent locks.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCross-entity effects go through a command buffer\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003eSimCommand\u003c/code\u003e). A\nphase reads world state and writes commands; the next phase applies\nthem. Deterministic, no mid-phase write conflicts.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe full tick phase order, ownership model, and feedback loops are\ndiagrammed in \u003ca href=\"/Kalcode/spaceprojectsim/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md\"\u003edocs/ARCHITECTURE.md\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe original \u003cstrong\u003eGodot\u003c/strong\u003e client lives on in history as a parity reference,\nbut it's no longer the front end — the pivot to an embedded Bevy client\nremoved the socket boundary <div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h1 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">🚀 The Space Project</h1><a id="user-content--the-space-project" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 🚀 The Space Project" href="#-the-space-project"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><strong>A self-running space-economy simulator, in Rust + Bevy.</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">Hundreds of autonomous ships trade, mine, haul cargo, take out contracts,
run out of fuel, and occasionally go bankrupt across a living solar
economy — markets find their own prices, factions tax and subsidize,
populations migrate when they're unhappy, and abandoned stations rot.
It all runs in one native binary with no runtime dependencies.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">What is this?</h2><a id="user-content-what-is-this" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: What is this?" href="#what-is-this"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The Space Project is an <strong>agent-driven economic simulation</strong> wrapped in a
native 3D client. There's no scripted storyline and no player objective —
you're an observer (and god-mode admin) watching an economy run itself.</p>
<p dir="auto">Every ship is an autonomous agent with its own credits, crew, fuel, cargo
hold, and a <strong>GOAP planner</strong> that decides what to do next: chase the
highest-margin trade route, accept a delivery contract, seek out a
shipyard to retrofit, or dock and let its crew rest before morale
collapses. Facilities run production recipes, degrade and self-repair,
level up, and get abandoned when they go broke. Factions collect taxes
and post subsidies. Populations consume food, produce labor, and pack up
and leave when sentiment craters. Markets price everything off a coverage
model with shortage urgency multipliers — no fixed prices anywhere.</p>
<p dir="auto">It started as an Elixir/Phoenix prototype and was rewritten in Rust
because the BEAM scheduler struggled on Windows gaming PCs. The engine
(<code>sim_core</code>) is pure, synchronous, IO-free Rust; the Bevy client embeds
it directly as a library, so the simulation and the renderer share the
same ECS world with zero marshalling between them.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Scale today:</strong> ~485 live agents (282 ships · 93 facilities · 27
populations · 8 factions · 60 celestial bodies), ticking at p50 ≈ 10–20 ms
inside a 125 ms budget. The architecture is built to push toward 100k+.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">🌌 A note on where this is going</h2><a id="user-content--a-note-on-where-this-is-going" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 🌌 A note on where this is going" href="#-a-note-on-where-this-is-going"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Nowhere, on its own — and that's kind of the point.</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">This started as a fun idea: a from-scratch space economy that actually
simulates itself instead of faking it. It grew <em>way</em> past what I
expected, mostly in late-night sessions pairing with Claude. But I'm
not pretending it's a game with a roadmap, and I'm not actively pushing
it toward "shippable."</p>
<p dir="auto">I'm putting it out under MIT because the bones are genuinely good and I'd
rather someone do something with it than let it sit in a private repo.
So: <strong>fork it, gut it, rename it, bolt a game on top of it, rip the
economy engine out and use it somewhere else entirely.</strong> Build the thing
I didn't.</p>
<p dir="auto">PRs and issues are welcome and I'll look at them, but I can't promise a
cadence. If you want to take it somewhere real, see
<a href="/Kalcode/spaceprojectsim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md">CONTRIBUTING.md</a> — there's a "directions you could
take this" section written exactly for you.</p>
</blockquote>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">What it simulates</h2><a id="user-content-what-it-simulates" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: What it simulates" href="#what-it-simulates"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>System</th>
<th>What happens</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Ship AI (GOAP)</strong></td>
<td>A forward planner scores every goal — trade, deliver, refuel, retrofit, rest, explore — over an abstract world state, then builds a behavior tree to execute the cheapest plan. Ships replan mid-flight when a better option appears.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Economy</strong></td>
<td>An order-book market per station prices 13 commodities off a coverage model with shortage-urgency multipliers. Ships move real supply between markets as they trade.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Contracts</strong></td>
<td>Six kinds — Delivery, Courier, Passenger, Subsidy, Supply, CrewMission — with a full posted → accepted → paid lifecycle, reputation gating, auto-renewal, and age-escalating payments.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Facilities</strong></td>
<td>Run production recipes (smelting, refining, manufacturing, farming, mining), degrade over time, self-repair with tools, level up 1–10, restock from local markets, and get abandoned when chronically broke.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Factions</strong></td>
<td>Collect taxes on member facilities, post subsidy contracts for chronic shortages, fund construction of new facilities where demand is unmet, and hold pairwise relations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Populations</strong></td>
<td>Consume food and fuel, produce labor, post food and passenger contracts under stress, and physically migrate to happier systems when sentiment collapses.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Crew</strong></td>
<td>Aggregate hunger / fatigue / morale with derived tasks (piloting, engineering, trading, eating, resting), skill progression, wages, and a morale death-spiral guard.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Construction</strong></td>
<td>Chronic shortages spawn construction sites that accrete delivered cargo 0 → 1.0, then materialize into a real, persistent facility.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Persistence</strong></td>
<td>Everything flushes to SQLite; a sim resumes from the exact tick it left off. A per-universe <code>world_seed</code> keeps the nebula backdrop and landmarks stable across restarts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Spatial LOD</strong></td>
<td>Distant ships tick less often (with rate-scaled state changes) so the frame budget goes where you're looking.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto">For the deep dive — tick phase ordering, the AI stack, the economic
feedback loop, runtime ownership — see
<a href="/Kalcode/spaceprojectsim/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md">docs/ARCHITECTURE.md</a>, which has mermaid diagrams
for all of it.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Architecture</h2><a id="user-content-architecture" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Architecture" href="#architecture"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Five crates in one Cargo workspace:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="sim_core     Pure simulation logic — hecs ECS, GOAP planner, economy,
             contracts. No async, no IO, no framework. Trivially testable.
sim_db       SQLite persistence (sqlx) — pool, seeder, ECS loader,
             persistence worker, migrations.
sim_server   Library crate — HTTP/WebSocket handlers + engine apply
             helpers. Drives headless mode; embedded by the client.
sim_protocol WebSocket wire types (headless / CI only).
client_bevy  The binary. Bevy 0.18 + egui. Embeds sim_core as a Bevy
             Resource; the renderer queries the hecs world directly."><pre class="notranslate"><code>sim_core     Pure simulation logic — hecs ECS, GOAP planner, economy,
             contracts. No async, no IO, no framework. Trivially testable.
sim_db       SQLite persistence (sqlx) — pool, seeder, ECS loader,
             persistence worker, migrations.
sim_server   Library crate — HTTP/WebSocket handlers + engine apply
             helpers. Drives headless mode; embedded by the client.
sim_protocol WebSocket wire types (headless / CI only).
client_bevy  The binary. Bevy 0.18 + egui. Embeds sim_core as a Bevy
             Resource; the renderer queries the hecs world directly.
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Three rules keep it honest:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><strong><code>sim_core</code> never imports tokio, sqlx, or axum.</strong> Pure logic only, so
the whole simulation is reasoned about and unit-tested without async.</li>
<li><strong>hecs is the source of truth during a tick.</strong> The tick loop holds
exclusive mutable access — no per-agent locks.</li>
<li><strong>Cross-entity effects go through a command buffer</strong> (<code>SimCommand</code>). A
phase reads world state and writes commands; the next phase applies
them. Deterministic, no mid-phase write conflicts.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">The full tick phase order, ownership model, and feedback loops are
diagrammed in <a href="/Kalcode/spaceprojectsim/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md">docs/ARCHITECTURE.md</a>.</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto">The original <strong>Godot</strong> client lives on in history as a parity reference,
but it's no longer the front end — the pivot to an embedded Bevy client
removed the socket boundary entirely, and every feature now lands in
<code>client_bevy</code>.</p>
</blockquote>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Building & packaging</h2><a id="user-content-building--packaging" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Building & packaging" href="#building--packaging"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="make build              # release binary (host target)

make build-mac          <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> arm64 macOS  (also: build-mac-intel, build-mac-universal)</span>
make build-win          <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Windows MSVC (run on a Windows host)</span>
make build-linux        <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Linux        (best on a Linux host)</span>

make package-mac        <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> .app bundle + ad-hoc codesign + Info.plist</span>
make dmg                <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> macOS .dmg</span>

<p dir="auto">The workspace version in the root <code>Cargo.toml</code> is the single source of
truth — the binary reads it via <code>env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")</code> and the
<code>Makefile</code> greps the same field for <code>Info.plist</code> and archive names, so
packaged builds never drift.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Tech stack</h2><a id="user-content-tech-stack" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Tech stack" href="#tech-stack"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong><a href="https://www.rust-lang.org/" rel="nofollow">Rust</a></strong> (edition 2021) — the whole thing</li>

<li><strong><a href="https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx">sqlx</a></strong> + SQLite — persistence, bundled so there's no runtime dependency</li>
<li><strong><a href="https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum">axum</a></strong> + tokio — the headless HTTP/WebSocket harness</li>
